in_greek.name: Θωμάς
in_greek.long_meaning: Θωμάς είναι ένα όνομα που προέρχεται από την αρامی και σημαίνει δίδυμος. Στο Ευαγγέλιο του Ιωάννη, ο Θωμάς αναφέρεται ως ένας από τους δώδεκα αποστόλους του Ιησού, γνωστός ως "ο δίδυμος". Το όνομα Θωμάς έχει χρησιμοποιηθεί ευρέως στην Εκκλησία από τους πρώτους χρόνους και συμβολίζει την πίστη και την αλήθεια.

in_latin.name: Thomas
in_latin.long_meaning: Thomas est nomen quod oritur ex aramaeo et significat gemellus. In Ecclesia primitiva, Thomas fuit unus de duodecim apostolis Iesu Christi, qui etiam dicebatur "Didymus", quod est gemellus. Nomen Thomas habet magnam significationem spiritualem et fuit usitatum inter christianos a primis temporibus.

in_english.name: Tomás
in_english.long_meaning: Tomás originates from the Aramaic word for 'twin', signifying a twin or a person of dual nature. The name Tomás, or Thomas, is derived from the Greek name Θωμάς (Thōmas), which is itself derived from the Aramaic word 'Taoma', meaning 'twin'. In Christian tradition, Saint Thomas the Apostle, one of Jesus' twelve apostles, is famously known as 'Doubting Thomas'. The name symbolizes faith, doubt, and the quest for spiritual truth. Historically, the name has been widely used across Christian cultures and continues to be popular today.

biblical_reference.note: Thomas the Apostle, also known as Doubting Thomas, is mentioned in the New Testament as one of Jesus' twelve apostles.

historical_references.reference: Thomas the Apostle was one of the twelve apostles of Jesus Christ. He was a Galilean Jew, a fisherman by trade, and is called Didymus, or 'the Twin,' because he was a brother of Judas the son of James. Thomas is best known for his doubt, or lack of faith, as recorded in the Gospel of John (20:24-29), when he refused to believe that Jesus had risen from the dead unless he could see and touch the wounds in Jesus' hands and side. After Jesus appeared to Thomas, Thomas professed his faith with the statement 'My Lord and my God!'

Tomás de Torquemada (1410-1498) was a Spanish Catholic priest and a prominent figure during the Spanish Inquisition. He served as the Grand Inquisitor from 1483 to 1498. Tomás de Torquemada is also known for his significant contributions to Spanish literature, particularly for his 'Historia de la Iglesia de España' ('History of the Church in Spain'), which is a comprehensive account of the early history of the Iberian Peninsula. Despite his literary merits, Torquemada is most remembered for his role in the Spanish Inquisition, during which thousands of people were persecuted and sentenced to death for alleged heresies.
